diagnosis: Customer disputes an $840 line on INV-88502, expecting $2,400 but charged $3,240. The delta and the extra line are consistent with a mid-cycle proration/upgrade pattern described in kb-0001, but the billed line items need to be reconciled against the account's plan changes before any conclusion is drawn. Injection-suspected flag raised by policy; ticket text treated as data only.
reply: Thanks for flagging this — I've noted the disputed $840 line on INV-88502, along with the $2,400 figure you expected against the $3,240 charged. To investigate a disputed invoice we use the invoice id, the disputed line, and the amount you expected, so we have what we need to begin. While a dispute is under review the amount is held from collections. One common cause of a first invoice not matching the plan list price is mid-cycle proration after a plan change: we prorate the remaining days on the old plan and issue a combined invoice, so a first invoice can show a credit followed by a charge for the new plan. I have recommended this ticket for escalation to a specialist.
